title: Which horn Lester played: alto in the 1920s, tenor later
summary: Phillips says Lester learned all these solos on alto, could play soprano and tenor too, and went back to alto in 1930 before taking up tenor again after Minneapolis.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Lester at this time was playing alto mainly, or was it tenor?
Alto.
So he was learning all these solos on alto?
Mmm-hmm. It didn't make no difference. He could play them on any horn.
Right. But I'm just wondering what he was playing most of the time.
Oh, he was playing mostly alto then.
But did he play the others horns, too, at that same time? I know he could have.
No, he was dealing with the alto.
So all this stuff you're telling me, was it...
Alto.
Were any of these solos on tenor?
No. All of them were alto.
Did he ever play C-melody at that time?
He never did bother with it too much, but he played it sometimes. He didn't bother with the C-melody.
Phillips - 67
He played the tenor, alto and the soprano.
Right. But the solos, as you say...
Yeah, he played them on the alto. He could play them on the tenor the same way, but at that time he was just playing alto.
I gather that later on he used to do some of these solos on tenor.

Yeah, I imagine. I don't know. It's kind of faded out. The time when he started playing tenor, you know, regularly... Well, there wasn't nobody playing that kind of music; I mean, playing those kind of solos. When he started playing tenor... He didn't start playing tenor until he got with the Blue Devils. He played it, but he'd quit playing tenor and went back to alto. Because when he left us and went to Minneapolis, he was playing alto. See, he went up there playing with... What's the piano player's name?
When he left Bronson in Minneapolis?
No, when he left us and went to... He left Bronson to go to Minneapolis.
Oh, when he left Art Bronson to go to Minneapolis. That's getting ahead of us. But that's when he started concentrating on tenor.
When he first... He left Bronson and went home at first, went back to his Dad. Well, he was playing tenor then. But when he went back down there, he started
Phillips - 68
playing alto.
When he went back to his father.
Yeah. Then, when he came back to us... He came back to us in 1930.
Back to Bronson.
Back to Bronson in 1930. And he was playing alto. Then he left us in 1930. He came to us in the Spring of 1930, and in the Fall of 1930, in Scott's Bluff, Nebraska, he left us.
What was he playing?
Alto.
And when did he leave Bronson?
That's getting ahead, but let's just finish on that point before we go back. What are you saying about the tenor? After that point, what was he playing?
Tenor. He started playing tenor after he went to Minneapolis. He went to Minneapolis to pick up on the tenor then. He got started playing tenor again.
As he got onto it again.
